# Day 1 — "Population: 1"

**Status:** final, rendered 2026-10-28 → `out/day1.mp4` (60.0 s, 1080×1920, 30 fps), cover `out/cover.png`.
**Code:** `day1.py` (camera, story, text, sound), `engine.py` (world), `narrate.py` (voice).
**Logline:** One person, alone in an empty valley, builds a tent and a fire, while the world shows what it could become.
**Feeling:** wonder, then quiet loneliness, ending on an open invitation.
**Hook rule shown:** 1 follower = 1 villager. **Open question planted:** the city at 1,000. **Ask:** "Comment: what do you want the world to have?"

# Day 3 — "It moved" (director's treatment, draft 2: tuned for the Reels algorithm)

## Why this draft changed (the evidence)
**Our numbers** (Instagram insights, read 2026-10-29):
| reel | views | viewers | views/viewer | non-followers | likes | comments | saves | shares | follows | follows/viewer |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Day 1 | 353 | 249 | 1.42 | 87 % | 19 | 9 | 2 | 0 | 11 | 4.4 % |
| Day 2 | 1,627 | 1,355 | 1.20 | 97 % | 60 | 24 | 20 | **0** | 39 | 2.9 % |

- Almost everyone who sees us is a stranger (97 %), so **frame 1 must explain the channel** to someone who has
  never heard of it. Day 2's frame 1 said "DAY 2 / SOMETHING WOKE UP", which only makes sense to followers.
- People who watch do follow (2.9-4.4 % is strong) and save (20). **Nobody shares (0).** Sends per reach is the
  signal that carries a reel to new people, so this is the gap to close.
- Rewatches fell from 1.42 to 1.20 views per viewer as the reel got longer and busier. (Average watch time and the
  retention graph are only in the phone app; they would tell us exactly where people leave.)

**The reference channel** (@realm.of.many, 7.4 K followers, same concept): normal reels get 5-16 K views. Their one
breakout (200 K, "Day 2, part 2") is **26 s long**, opens with the payoff as a number ("6 followers → 6 cabins")
over the whole village, then shows each new house with its owner's handle, "new since Part 1: @name", and the
comment wish ("wish by @darkgeniuses: palisade — started"). Its caption ends "Find your house: link in bio" (they
run a website at realmofmany.github.io). Its top comments are people asking for **their own** home type
("Can I have a Blacksmith's house :D?" 1,059 ♥, "may i have a wizards tower" 148 ♥).

**What Instagram ranks Reels on** (Mosseri, Jan 2025, still repeated in 2026 guides): watch time / completion,
sends per reach, likes per reach. Sends matter most for reaching non-followers.

## The director's rules for Day 3, from that
1. **Frame 1 = the rule + the payoff number + motion.** A stranger reads "1 FOLLOWER = 1 VILLAGER" and
   "42 FOLLOWED → 42 HOMES" while something big moves. The rule stays as a small strip under the HUD all the way
   through, for anyone who joins mid-reel.
2. **Shorter: 38 s instead of 60.** Completion and rewatches count more than length. Every beat 2-4 s, a visible
   change at least every 2 s.
3. **Built to be rewatched:** the 42 handles roll by too fast to read in one go ("FIND YOUR NAME 👀"), so people
   pause or replay. The last frame cuts cleanly into the first.
4. **Built to be sent:** personal payoffs people want to show a friend (your name on a house, your wish came true),
   one funny character (the hunchback who waves at everyone), and one jaw-drop image (the dragon's face, the
   black hole, the totems lighting up). One soft line near the end: "SEND THIS TO YOUR FUTURE NEIGHBOUR".
5. **Comments with a personal stake:** show that people who asked to *be* something got it (blacksmith, wizard,
   knight, vampire), so the next viewers comment "can I be…?". The spoken ask stays the canon line.
6. **Sound off still works:** every beat reads from the words on screen; the narrator is shorter and lighter.

- 52 followers → **POP 53**, 42 new villagers, @keelinbb unfollowed.
- Top comment @darrellrasor42 "Enchanted Tiki Island" **7♥** → an original tiki lagoon copied from the owner's
  reference with **no** SpongeBob characters and no SpongeBob name on screen.

  goes into the world; the wanderer (@carlossgarciaah) is a hunchback; the caped villager (@gulalireng) is a vampire
  who turns into a bat and only shows at night; names are shown, not read out; the wizard tower (@huntman225) has a

# Day 3 — "Something waved back" (story cut, draft 3)

A re-cut of Day 3 that uses only what is already built and in the world (the structure, the vampire → bat, the
dragon's embers and the HD dragon, the castle, the knight, the street of 39 homes, the wish homes, the fishing hut
and boat, the tiki lagoon and its totems, the hunchback, the hooded figure). No new models. Same 38 s,
1080×1920. It replaces the narration, the words on screen and a few character placements of `SCRIPT.md`
("It moved", as rendered).

## Why re-cut: what the rendered cut does and where it loses people
Read from `out/day3_strip.png` (1 frame/s) against what Instagram ranks on.
1. **Frame 1 is a number, not a question.** "42 FOLLOWED → 42 HOMES" tells a stranger the result before they care.
   97 % of our viewers are strangers (Day 2 insights), and Instagram now counts viewers who skip in the first 3 s.
2. **12–26 s is a catalogue.** A list card, then seven "ASKED TO BE A …" cuts. Each cut is a label, so nothing pulls
   the viewer into the next one. This is the longest stretch of the reel and the one most likely to lose people.
3. **No one to follow.** The story is about "the world", so there is no character to root for or send to a friend.
4. **The ending is not earned.** The hooded figure appears for the first time at 33 s with no link to anything
   before it, so "Someone is watching" has no setup.
5. **Weak send prompt.** "Send this to your future neighbour" names nobody. Day 2 got **0 shares**, and shares
   (sends per reach) are what carry a reel to new people.

## The fix: one hero, one chain, one threat
- **Hero: the hunchback (@carlossgarciaah)**, the stranger who didn't want a house, only to say hi to everyone.
  It's already built and waving, it's funny, and everyone has a friend like that (the send).
- **The catalogue becomes a walk.** The hunchback says hi to each wish home and each one answers in its own way
  (anvil sparks, the black hole pulses, the knight's armour clanks, the oar splashes, the basement hatch creaks
  open). Same credits, but now every cut is a step in a story.
- **The threat pays off the hero's habit.** The hunchback waves at the far tower, and the hooded figure waves back.
  That's the cliffhanger, and the theory bait for Day 4.
- **Every line causes the next** (skill rule): strangers came → the tower sank → one stranger isn't human →
  sunrise: the dragon changed → the tower came back → homes for everyone → one stranger didn't want a home → it
  said hi to everyone → everyone said hi back → even the totems → it waved at the tower → something waved back.

Read alone, without pictures, the narration tells the whole story:
> Forty-two strangers moved in. The tower... didn't like it. One of them... isn't human. At sunrise, the dragon
> shed its skin. And far away... the tower came back. We built forty-two homes. Find yours. One stranger didn't
> want a house... only to say hi to everyone. And everyone said hi back. The top comment wished for a tiki island.
> Even its totems said hi. Then the hunchback waved at the tower. Something... waved back. Comment: what do you
> want the world to have?

85 words in 38 s (about 2.2 words a second), with silence under the dragon, the rise and the walk.

## Shot list (38 s)

The single source of truth for what exists in the world and where. Every day's script starts from the
"State after the last day" below and, when its reel is final, adds a new state block. Day scripts live in
`dayN/SCRIPT.md`.

## Fixed forever (changing these changes the whole world)
- The world is generated from fixed seeds in `engine.py` (copied into each day's folder unchanged except for
  additive fields): `WORLD = 800`, camp centre **C = (400, 400)**, river, trees, rocks, grass and clouds come out
  identical every run. Never edit seeds, `WORLD`, `CX0/CY0` or the river formula.

  the giant structure ~62, the dragon ~66 long with ~90 wingspan.
